newsitem.title: USA: Motorola debt off a bit on earnings warning.
newsitem.headline: Motorola debt off a bit on earnings warning.

text.p: Motorola Inc long-term debt inched lower on Wednesday after the company said its projected third quarter earnings could fall 25 percent or more from the previous period, dealers said.

The yield spread on the 7-1/2 percent debentures due 2025 was quoted from unchanged to two basis points wider by various high-grade corporates dealers. The paper closed on Tuesday at a 51 bid, 48 offered basis point spread over Treasuries.
"There's no question the paper is weaker, but only a few issues actively trade and it wasn't as if the news was a total surprise," one industrials dealer said.
Standard & Poor's analyst Bruce Hyman said the news would have no immediate impact on the firm's ratings or outlook and no official statement in reaction to the news was planned.

When asked if the earnings warning would hurt Motorola's credit rating, Hyman replied: "No it won't, neither on the (short-term) paper nor on the long-term. We had already looked into it and, frankly, we're not totally shocked by the fact that it couldn't turn the semiconductor business around."
In a statement issued earlier, Motorola blamed the weaker earnings outlook in particular on its semiconducter business.
Motorola's senior unsecured debt is rated double-A by S&P and Aa3 by Moody's Investors Service Inc.
Motorola shares were down 1-5/8 at 49 in mid-morning trade.
According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' estimates for the third quarter was $0.50 a share. The company earned $0.54 a share in the second quarter.
